audit_findings.title: Post-anchor borrowing may create interest expense absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt increased $54.006 million from $709.890 million at 2025-12-31 to $763.896 million at 2026-06-30; six-month interest expense increased $1.344 million, equal to 2.7% of the $49.6 million OE anchor; future effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher post-anchor interest expense reduces equity-level OE because debt principal is not separately deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: However, the Company anticipates to increase its existing debt capacity over the coming years to further support the increased cash requirements for operations and capital expenditures associated with the natural colors conversion activity.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher debt balance and increased interest expense are demonstrated, but the June 2026 filing also contemplates further borrowing whose amount, timing, and rate are unknown. The observed interest increase alone is small relative to the anchor, while the unquantified future borrowing prevents establishing the total valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Build a debt and interest schedule from the June 2026 debt balance, current rates, planned refinancing, the undrawn $400 million facility, and conversion-program funding needs; rerun every scenario with incremental after-tax interest in OE.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling does not capture maximum PSU dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: Absolute conservative bound of 2.320 million additional shares above the included 0.580 million pool, increasing the 43.142811 million denominator by at most 5.4% and reducing base value from $16.87 to approximately $16.01 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Maximum PSU settlements increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the December 2025 performance stock grant to elected officers, enhanced payout levels were included to allow for additional payouts up to 2.5 times the 200 % payout level, if the stated enhanced performance criteria are met.
audit_findings.explanation: Calling the current denominator a maximum ceiling is unsupported because enhanced officer PSUs can pay up to five times target. Nevertheless, even the deliberately extreme assumption that every unit in the entire 0.580 million pool receives that multiplier reduces per-share value by only about 5.1%; the actual effect must be smaller because the pool includes fixed restricted shares and awards with lower multipliers. This cannot change the conclusion relative to the $134.84 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain award-level target units and payout caps and replace the provisional denominator with the exact maximum issuable share count; no aggregate valuation rerun is needed beyond updating per-share outputs.

audit_findings.title: Natural-color growth may require more reinvestment than the forecast charges
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 capital expenditures were $67.513 million versus $38.035 million in first-half 2025, a $29.478 million increase; inventories used $42.811 million of cash versus $0.548 million, and net debt increased $62.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Capacity capital expenditures and incremental working capital reduce OE supporting the 3%-5% growth cases; crediting growth before those outlays earn returns overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Because much more natural color is generally needed to replicate the appearance of a synthetic color in an existing product, this conversion activity presents major opportunities for the Company and requires increased commercial and R&D activity to support customers and significant investment around the world to increase the Company’s production capacity, optimize and expand its product portfolio, and build a resilient supply chain.
audit_findings.explanation: The increased investment burden is demonstrated and is large relative to the $49.6 million OE anchor. What remains unresolved is whether the scenario reinvestment formula already captures the full conversion-program spending. Given the filed spending and the stated 3.5% return on new tangible assets, any omission is reasonably capable of materially reducing the base and bull valuations.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each scenario's annual reinvestment charge to conversion-related capital expenditures, inventory and receivable requirements, project timing, and the 3.5% return assumption; rerun base and bull cases with growth deferred until the associated investment produces OE.

audit_findings.title: Defined-benefit funding may be an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Expected 2026 contribution of $5.1 million, equal to 10.3% of the $49.6 million OE anchor; funded deficit of $14.548 million, equal to 29.3% of the anchor and 2.0% of $728 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash contributions exceeding pension expense reduce OE, or the unfunded obligation may require a separate equity-bridge claim if not already captured.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to contribute $ 5.1 million to defined benefit plans in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The contribution and deficit are filed amounts, but the record does not show whether the OE calculation already captures pension cash funding or whether the $5.1 million contribution is recurring. The bridge-scale deficit is only about 2% of base equity value, while sustained contribution gaps could be more consequential; materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile pension expense, cash contributions, and cash-flow-statement treatment within OE; obtain projected contributions and benefit payments, then either charge incremental funding in OE or deduct the funded deficit in the bridge, but not both.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain restructuring costs that are ending
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 plan costs were $15.806 million pre-tax, including $5.297 million identified as non-cash and $10.509 million of employee-separation, production, and other costs; the latter equals 21.2% of the $49.6 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring cash costs retained in the anchor depress starting OE and all discounted projections; non-cash charges should affect OE only according to the anchor construction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has substantially completed all other actions contemplated under the Portfolio Optimization Plan in accordance with local laws.
audit_findings.explanation: Completion is demonstrated: the company reported no plan costs in first-half 2026 and stated that all actions were complete. Whether the $49.6 million anchor retained each charge is unresolved, but the potentially retained cash-associated amount is large enough to change the valuation materially. The separate projected $8 million annual savings should not be added unless absent from the post-plan operating base.
audit_findings.action: Trace every FY2025 plan-cost component through net income, operating cash flow, and the OE calculation; remove only verified nonrecurring cash costs, handle non-cash charges consistently, and rerun all scenarios without separately double-counting the disclosed $8 million savings.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat required liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum bridge overstatement is the full $31.019 million, or $0.72 per share and 4.3% of the $728 million base equity value; removing all cash would reduce base value from $16.87 to approximately $16.15 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only distributable excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; operating, restricted, or investment-program cash must remain in the business.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects its cash flow from operations and its existing debt capacity can be used to meet anticipated future cash requirements for operations, capital expenditures, and dividend payments, as well as potential acquisitions and stock repurchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish that all cash is excess, but the entire possible error is bounded by the filed balance. Even removing every dollar would leave estimated value far below the $134.84 market price and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash, jurisdictional restrictions, repatriation costs, and committed near-term conversion spending; update the bridge with only verified excess cash.
